name: Offline machine translation of a non-English transcript with a synth/DAW glossary
goal: Turn an original-language Show-transcript (es, de, ja, fr, pt, it) into an English transcript with a free offline translator (argos-translate), segment by segment with the original timestamps. Fix known domain mistranslations after translating ('envolvente' rendered as 'cover' -> 'envelope'), reject garbled model output, and keep the original words. Delta vs generic translation skills (azure-ai-translation-*, translate-book): offline and free, timestamp-preserving for transcripts, with a post-edit glossary for sound-design vocabulary and a garble detector.
prerequisites: Language packs installed: translate_transcript.py --install-langs de,es,ja,fr,pt,it (es is pinned to package 1.0)

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: Source language code (taken from the filename if omitted)

outputs.name: english_transcript
outputs.description: raw/<id>/transcript.txt with a '# MACHINE-TRANSLATED ...' header and the original timestamps

outputs.name: translation_report
outputs.description: raw/<id>/translation.json: backend, segment count, glossary hits, per-segment domain terms, garbled_share, seconds

constraints: Transcript source is YouTube's Show transcript panel text (info section -> Transcript); say 'transcript', not 'captions'. Caption-file transports (.srt/.vtt) are only used internally and deleted.
Never invent transcript text, steps, or settings; every downstream fact must trace to a transcript timestamp.
No Whisper/ASR on the audio unless Matt explicitly asks; the router may only FLAG it as a last resort.

Always mark machine-translated text as such (header line + meta.translated=true + translation_method 'machine:<backend>'); skills distilled from it must say so in source and cross-check numbers against the original words.

Do not inject English terms into the source before translating. Tested 2026-10-03: argos produced garbage when English words were mixed into Spanish input. Correct terms only after translation, and only when the source segment contains the term.

argos es->en package 1.9 outputs garbage with argostranslate 1.11 / ctranslate2 4.8; use the pinned 1.0 package. The garble detector (more than 20% of segments with foreign-script junk) stops the run and writes nothing.
Paid cloud translators are not used unless Matt sets one up; the backend registry makes adding one a single function.

steps.action: Parse the original panel into (timestamp, text) rows, skipping '#' lines. Group consecutive auto-track fragments under the first timestamp until about 160 characters or end punctuation (ja/zh joined without spaces), so the model sees whole clauses.
steps.expect: Fewer, longer segments, each keeping its first timestamp

steps.action: Translate each segment with the chosen backend (argos: installed language -> get_translation('en').translate). Exactly one output per input segment; a count mismatch fails the run.
steps.expect: English segment list the same length as the input

steps.action: Post-edit: for each glossary term present in the source segment (lexicons/translation_glossary.json: lang -> term -> [english, known bad renderings]), replace known bad renderings in the output with the English term, unless that rendering is the correct English for another term in the same segment.
steps.expect: 'cover attack' -> 'envelope attack'; per-segment term list recorded

steps.action: Run the garble check. If more than 20% of output segments contain CJK/Hangul/Greek-range junk, return mt_output_garbled and write nothing; the router then stops with STOP_translation_failed.
steps.expect: Garbled output never reaches the graph

steps.action: Write transcript.txt (header + timestamps + English), raw.txt and raw (English prose), and translation.json. Leave transcript.orig.<lang>.txt untouched.
steps.expect: Original and English side by side

steps.action: To add a backend, write _backend_x(segments, src, tgt) -> list[str] and register it in BACKENDS. To fix a recurring mistranslation, add the bad rendering to the glossary rather than editing outputs by hand.
steps.expect: Pluggable backends; glossary grows from evidence

verification: transcript.txt starts with '# MACHINE-TRANSLATED' and keeps the original timestamps
translation.json garbled_share <= 0.2 and segments == number of timestamp lines
